hero.headline: MESSI'S ELEVEN-MINUTE MIRACLE
hero.standfirst: Two goals down with eleven minutes left, a penalty already missed — and then Argentina scored three times to break Egypt's hearts, Messi taking the Golden Boot lead in the middle of it. In Vancouver, Switzerland and Colombia needed penalties after 120 goalless minutes, and Gregor Kobel sent the Swiss into a first quarter-final in 72 years.
hero.photoCaption: Lionel Messi — a missed penalty, an assist, and his 8th goal of the tournament, all in one night

briefing.text: Crystal Ball, day two: Argentina called correctly (if far less comfortably than predicted); Colombia didn't land — though the verdict did warn of penalties in Vancouver.
Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shoubir saved a Messi penalty and led 2–0 with 11 minutes left — the fairy tale died very, very hard.
No football today. The quarter-finals begin Thursday: France–Morocco in Boston, then one tie a day through Sunday.

facts.text: Goalkeeper Mostafa Shoubir saved Messi's first-half penalty — and Egypt led 2–0 until the 79th minute
Messi's 83rd-minute strike was his 8th of the tournament — the outright Golden Boot lead
Argentina scored three times in 13 minutes after going 25 games' worth of knockout pedigree into the red

yesterday.report: Egypt did everything but finish the job. Yasser Ibrahim's 15th-minute header from a corner, a Messi penalty pushed away by Mostafa Shoubir minutes later, and a second from Mostafa Ziko on 67 — the champions were two down, out of ideas, and out of time. Atlanta braced for the shock of the tournament.
yesterday.report2: Then Argentina remembered who they are. Cristian Romero headed in Messi's cross on 79, Messi swept in the equaliser on 83 — his eighth, and the Golden Boot lead — and Enzo Fernández completed the turnaround in stoppage time. Nineteen attempts to five tells you the pressure never stopped; champions simply refuse to lose until the maths says they must.

star.name: Lionel Messi
star.line: A saved penalty would have broken most players. Instead, at 39: the cross for Romero, the equaliser for the Golden Boot lead, and one more quarter-final. His tournament now runs through Switzerland on Sunday.

aside.name: Enzo Fernández
aside.line: The stoppage-time winner that turned a great escape into a statement. Argentina's engine room delivered when the legs of others had gone.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Argentina meet Switzerland in Sunday's Kansas City quarter-final (02:00 +1). Egypt exit their finest World Cup one hurdle short of history.

yesterday.stage: Round of 16 · QF4 slot · 0–0 aet, 4–3 pens

facts.text: Colombia's xG of 1.03 to 0.35 tells the story: Lucumí hit the crossbar and Campaz blazed over in extra time
Kobel saved Hernández's kick in the shootout; Akanji's own miss didn't matter in the end
Switzerland are in a World Cup quarter-final for the first time since 1954 — a 72-year wait

yesterday.report: Exactly the match the market predicted: 120 minutes, no goals, and the finest of margins. Colombia created what chances there were — Lucumí rattled the crossbar and Campaz fired over in extra time, their 1.03 xG dwarfing Switzerland's 0.35 — but the Swiss block never cracked, and the night went where it always felt destined to go.
yesterday.report2: In the shootout, Gregor Kobel dived to keep out Carlos Hernández's kick, and even Manuel Akanji's miss couldn't swing it back: Ruben Vargas swept in the winner for 4–3. Switzerland reach the last eight of a World Cup for the first time since 1954, and Colombia go home having lost, in the truest sense, to nobody.

star.name: Gregor Kobel
star.line: A clean sheet through 120 minutes behind a creaking block, then the decisive save in the shootout. Switzerland's 72-year wait ended on his gloves.

aside.name: Ruben Vargas
aside.line: The man for the moment that mattered most — the winning penalty, buried without a flicker of doubt.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Switzerland meet Argentina in Sunday's Kansas City quarter-final. The reward for 120 minutes of discipline: the champions of the world.

today.preview: A rematch of the 2022 semi-final, and the tie of the round. France have cruised on Mbappé's seven goals and Dembélé's wing play; Morocco arrive as the best defensive side of the knockouts bar Spain, fresh from dismantling Canada 3–0. In 2022 they ran out of miracles against exactly this opponent — Thursday tells us if this squad is different.
watch: Mbappé, one behind Messi, against the defence that shut out Canada
Winner faces Spain or Belgium in Tuesday's Dallas semi-final

keyMan.name: Kylian Mbappé
keyMan.line: Seven goals, two assists, and the memory of 2022 — the last time Morocco stood between France and a semi-final, he was on the winning side.

today.preview: The tournament's meanest defence against its suddenly hottest attack. Spain have not conceded a single goal in five games; Belgium just put four past the hosts in their sharpest display in years. Something gives on Friday — and the winner will fancy themselves in the semi-final.
watch: Spain's five straight clean sheets against De Ketelaere's new-found ruthlessness

keyMan.name: Charles De Ketelaere
keyMan.line: Two goals against the USA announced him as Belgium's new tournament talisman. Now the hardest assignment in football: finding a way past a Spain defence that hasn't blinked in five games.
